correctness.rationale: For part i, a zero vertex is valid exactly when there is an external label 3 or at least two external labels 2, while a one vertex is valid exactly when there is an external label 2 or 3. The quasi-total condition is automatic when positive support meets two parts and otherwise forces all positives to be 2. The case split on 3-support and 2-support is therefore necessary and sufficient. The polynomial terms are disjoint translations of these cases. The definition-level checker verifies every coefficient over 58 multipartite types and 1,653,904 labelings through order eight.

value.rationale: QTDRD is an established optimization parameter with NP-hard decision complexity. On complete multipartite graphs, the theorem gives a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary slice: every feasible function is determined by defender-support concentration across parts. The exact weight enumerator records all feasible weights and multiplicities and exposes precisely how the quasi-total relaxation differs structurally from total double Roman domination.
